text: "Is this some kind of joke? If you are who you say you are, you're on several $faction wanted lists."
"You're already commissioned by $theOtherCommissionFaction. You'll have to resign that commission before you can be commissioned by $theFaction."
"I'm sorry, but you don't meet our criteria for receiving a commission."

"Hmm, yes, you're a suitable candidate.

Accepting a commission is a serious matter. You will be required to fight enemies of $theFaction, wherever they may be found.

You'll be able to resign your commission at any time, though I don't imagine doing so would win you any friends."
"So, how about it? Still want to sign on?"
"Excellent! Welcome to the service."
"Anything else I can do for you?"
"Yes, not everyone has it in them to uphold the values of $theFaction to such a high standard. No shame in it.\n\nAnything else I can do for you?"
"Are you sure? $TheFaction needs people it can rely on, and turning your back like this won't be easily forgotten."
"I can see there's no changing your mind. Well, at least you had the courtesy to tender your resignation in person."
"A good decision. We can use people like you."

script:
SetTextHighlightColors textGreenColor textGreenColor highlight
SetTextHighlights "Executing transfer..." "Maelstrom blueprint" "\"Not bad.\""
DASubject71_TransferVirtuous
text:
Executing transfer...

An active drive field signature is detected from the fleet. Your security officer instinctively moves his hand towards the alert switch, but after a second glance towards the sensors, moves it away.

The Virtuous mech approaches your fleet and another message appears on the display.
The archive contains a Maelstrom blueprint.

The Last Line pings your IFF codes back to you. One line has been added: "Not bad."

Disconnecting...
The comm link closes and the display goes black.

A security team enters the Virtuous. On the tactical display, you see the doors open to the bridge autonomously, where a mess of hanging wires and disconnected life support systems surround a husk of a corpse. The team lead checks its vitals and reports it as deceased.

After another few minutes, the security team clears the Virtuous, with no other signs of life aboard the ship.

script:
ShowDefaultVisual
PrintDescription 3
Highlight "FIRST RELAY"
SetShortcut defaultLeave ESCAPE

ShowDefaultVisual
Highlight "FIRST RELAY" "signal" "Gulf"
SetShortcut defaultLeave ESCAPE
text:
The frame has fused and warped, exposing a gutted interior. Yet this fading echo of the Corporation remains in orbit.

By modern standards, its tolerances are finer, its internal geometry denser, and several structural joins nearly seamless.

Beneath the scars of micrometeorite impacts, faded white lettering still stands proudly against the scorched red hull:

FIRST RELAY

A survey team enters through the exposed section.

There are no bodies, no active reactors, and no intact escape craft.

Buried in the static, a signal persists. It carries the same outdated identification code as the transmission that pinged the Gulf.

Your comms officer runs the code again. Then a third time.
Neither the facility nor this system appears on any navigational chart or corporate registry.

script:
Highlight "Deep Strike Catapult" "extensive conversion" "rebuild a carrier" "Diable-pattern orbital station"
AddRemoveAnyItem SPECIAL modspec "gulf_deep_strike" 1
AddRemoveAnyItem SPECIAL industry_bp "diableavionics_orbitalstation" 1
$global.da_gulf_part2_complete = true
text:
Your overworked salvage team manages to recover a battle-worn Deep Strike Catapult from the wreck. Its internal data core is ancient but intact.

At first, it holds little of interest: firing data, launch codes, the Admiralty’s usual boilerplate. But deeper in the archive, your engineers discover that the weapon was only one component of a far more extensive conversion: structural alterations, power-routing requirements, fighter bay modifications, and the complete specifications for a long-forgotten EMP subsystem.

The Catapult was never intended to be installed alone. These schematics describe how to rebuild a carrier around it.

A separate archive contains complete construction specifications for a Diable-pattern orbital station, sufficient to reproduce the design without access to Corporation shipyards.
